sentences.en: From The New York Times, this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，这是《访谈》栏目。

sentences.en: I'm David Marchese.
sentences.zh: 我是大卫·马尔凯塞。

sentences.en: As the old saying goes, the only constant is change.
sentences.zh: 俗话说得好，唯一不变的就是变化。

sentences.en: Lately, though, the change can feel overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 然而最近，这种变化让人感到难以招架。

sentences.en: We are, after all, living through an era of widespread democratic backsliding, massive technological disruption,
sentences.zh: 毕竟，我们正经历一个民主广泛倒退、技术剧烈颠覆的时代，

sentences.en: and the ongoing slow-motion disaster of the climate crisis, to name just a few.
sentences.zh: 以及气候危机这场仍在缓慢进行中的灾难，这还只是其中几项。

sentences.en: But what if there was a different and more hopeful story to tell about all that upheaval?
sentences.zh: 但如果我们能对所有这些动荡讲述一个不同且更有希望的故事呢？

sentences.en: That's the question at the heart of The Beginning Comes After the End, the new book by the prolific and critically acclaimed writer Rebecca Solnit.
sentences.zh: 这就是多产且广受好评的作家丽贝卡·索尔尼特的新书《终点之后是起点》的核心问题。

sentences.en: A thematic sequel to her earlier classic, Hope in the Dark,
sentences.zh: 这是她早期经典之作《黑暗中的希望》的主题续篇，

sentences.en: The book takes a longer view on progress and offers a more optimistic philosophy of change based on ideas of interconnection, feminism, ecological care, and political equality.
sentences.zh: 这本书对进步采取了更长远的眼光，并基于互联性、女性主义、生态关怀和政治平等的理念，提供了一种更加乐观的变革哲学。

sentences.en: It's not a naive book.
sentences.zh: 这不是一本天真的书。

sentences.en: Solnit is keenly aware of the massive challenges we're all facing.
sentences.zh: 索尔尼特敏锐地意识到了我们所有人面临的巨大挑战。

sentences.en: But it provides a stabilizing counterweight to the feeling that the world has spun dangerously off-kilter.
sentences.zh: 但它为那种世界已经危险地严重失衡的感觉提供了一个稳定的平衡重锤。

sentences.en: Here's my conversation with Rebecca Solnit.
sentences.zh: 以下是我与丽贝卡·索尔尼特的对话。

sentences.en: You know, Rebecca, it's a real pleasure for me to speak to you, in part because A Field Guide to Getting Lost was a really big book for me,
sentences.zh: 你知道，丽贝卡，能和您交谈我真的很高兴，部分原因是因为《迷路指南》对我来说是一本非常重要的书，

sentences.en: and I read it not long after I had moved from my home in Toronto to New York City, and it felt like a real companion at the time.
sentences.zh: 我在从多伦多的家搬到纽约市后不久就读了它，当时它感觉像是一个真正的伴侣。

sentences.en: And just the way it captured the idea that displacement and a kind of solitude can actually be positive things.
sentences.zh: 它捕捉到流离失所和某种孤独实际上可以是积极的事情的那种方式。

sentences.en: So thank you for that.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你写了这本书。

sentences.en: I'm so glad you found it at the right time for you.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你在正确的时间遇到了它。

sentences.en: And yeah, that book, we just put out a 20th anniversary edition,
sentences.zh: 是的，那本书，我们刚刚推出了20周年纪念版，

sentences.en: and I got to spend some time revisiting it and rethinking what the hell it was I was doing in the early 2000s with it.
sentences.zh: 我花了一些时间重读它，并重新思考我在2000年代初写它的时候到底在搞什么鬼。

sentences.en: And it's been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I wrote that book, and then I wrote Hope in the Dark, and I thought, like, am I schizophrenic?
sentences.zh: 我写了那本书，然后写了《黑暗中的希望》，当时我想，我是精神分裂了吗？

sentences.en: These books are so different.
sentences.zh: 这些书太不一样了。

sentences.en: And then I realized that Hope in the Dark, which is very political and very upbeat, and A Field Guide to Getting Lost, which is introspective and kind of melancholy,
sentences.zh: 后来我意识到，《黑暗中的希望》非常具有政治性且非常乐观，而《迷路指南》则带有内省色彩且略显忧郁，

sentences.en: were both about coming to terms with uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 它们其实都是关于如何接受不确定性的。

sentences.en: But of course, I also wrote A Field Guide to Getting Lost, as I do a lot of my books, to kind of react against something happening in the culture.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我也和我的许多其他书一样，为了反抗文化中正在发生的一些事情而写了《迷路指南》。

sentences.en: And something that was already happening with tech was the idea that we want to live in a safe, circumscribed, known world.
sentences.zh: 科技当时已经在催生的一种观念是，我们希望生活在一个安全、狭隘、已知世界里。

sentences.en: We don't want to leave the house without knowing exactly where we're going in a sense that we need to be in control, that we need to know everything.
sentences.zh: 我们不想在不知道具体去哪里的情况下离开家，这种心态源于我们需要掌控一切，我们需要了解一切。

sentences.en: And of course, we're never completely in control and we never completely know everything.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们永远无法完全掌控一切，也永远无法完全了解一切。

sentences.en: So how do we look at it in a way that lets us accept it and maybe work with it instead of deny it or work against it?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该如何看待它，从而能够接受它并与之合作，而不是去否认它或对抗它呢？

sentences.en: What in the culture would you say your new book is reacting against?
sentences.zh: 你认为你的新书是在反抗文化中的什么现象？

sentences.en: Really a kind of cultural amnesia.
sentences.zh: 实际上是一种文化失忆症。

sentences.en: I think of time in increments of a year, five years, 50 years, centuries.
sentences.zh: 我以一年、五年、五十年、几个世纪为时间增量来思考时间。

sentences.en: And across that time span, you can really see how profoundly the world has changed and is changing.
sentences.zh: 跨越这个时间跨度，你真的能看到世界发生了多么深刻的改变，并且正在发生怎样的改变。

sentences.en: You can see that these good things, you know, feminism, civil rights movements, environmental awareness, indigenous resurgences have had a profound impact.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到这些美好的事物，你知道的，女性主义、民权运动、环境意识、原住民的复兴，都产生了深远的影响。

sentences.en: so often people seem to think in these very short-term intervals in which they either think
sentences.zh: 但人们往往倾向于用极短的时间间隔来思考，要么觉得

sentences.en: nothing has changed or they just see the last bad thing that happened and think we're losing
sentences.zh: 什么都没有改变，要么只看到了最近发生的一件坏事，就认为我们在节节败退，

sentences.en: so context is everything and I often feel that a lot of pessimism despair doomerism comes from
sentences.zh: 所以背景决定一切，我经常觉得许多悲观主义、绝望情绪和末日论都源于

sentences.en: not knowledge about the future even though they think they're thinking about the future but
sentences.zh: 对未来的无知，尽管他们以为自己是在思考未来，但实际上

sentences.en: from lack of knowledge about the paSt. Despair and amnesia go hand in hand, and so do hope and memory, I think, in many cases.
sentences.zh: 是对过去的无知。绝望和失忆形影不离，我认为，希望和记忆在许多情况下也是如此。

sentences.en: So when people are reading the news or thinking about changes from day to day or month to month or even year to year, and it's making them feel like they're just
sentences.zh: 因此，当人们在阅读新闻或思考日复一日、月复一月甚至年复一年的变化时，这让他们觉得他们只是

sentences.zh: 他们还应该具备什么额外的背景，来帮助他们拼凑出完整的画面，并向他们展示这些更深层的积极变革潮流？

sentences.en: I think even the right tells us something, if we listen very carefully to what they're saying, something very encouraging.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果我们非常仔细地倾听右翼在说什么，甚至连他们也能告诉我们一些非常鼓舞人心的事情。

sentences.en: They tell us, you all are very powerful.
sentences.zh: 他们在告诉我们，你们非常强大。

sentences.en: You've changed the world profoundly.
sentences.zh: 你们深刻地改变了世界。

sentences.en: all these things that are often treated separately feminism queer rights environmental and climate
sentences.zh: 所有这些通常被单独对待的事物——女性主义、酷儿权益、环境与气候

sentences.en: action ideas of equality etc are actually all connected so they're basically telling us we're
sentences.zh: 行动、平等理念等——其实都是相互关联的，所以他们基本上是在告诉我们，我们

sentences.en: incredibly successful which is the good news the bad news is they hate it and they want to change it all back.
sentences.zh: 取得了难以置信的巨大成功，这是好消息；坏消息是他们恨透了这一点，并希望把这一切都改回去。

sentences.en: So much of what we're seeing with Trumpism, with the far-right resurgence or surge right now, is a fury at how the world has been changed and a desire to change it back, to put
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到的特朗普主义、极右翼势力的复苏或高涨，很大程度上是对世界如何被改变的愤怒，以及想要改回去的渴望，想把

sentences.en: women back, you know, kind of barefoot, pregnant, and in the kitchen, to recreate racial hierarchies
sentences.zh: 女性重新变回，你知道的，那种围着灶台转、只管生孩子的状态，想重建

sentences.en: that have been dismantled to some extent, to impose Christianity, mandatory heterosexuality
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上已经被拆除的种族等级制度，强加基督教、强制异性恋，

sentences.en: and it's an anti-connection ideology and so there's a backlash it is significant but it is not comprehensive or global I was on book tour last year in Europe and the Europeans
sentences.zh: 这是一种反连接的意识形态，因此产生了强烈的反弹，它虽然不容忽视，但并非无所不包或全球性的。我去年在欧洲做图书巡回宣传时，欧洲人

sentences.zh: 让我大跌眼镜，他们竟然问：哦，罗诉韦德案被推翻了，这不意味着女性主义

sentences.en: has failed and I was like the United States is four percent of the population meanwhile all these
sentences.zh: 已经失败了吗？而我当时说，美国只占全球人口的4%

sentences.en: Catholic countries, Argentina, Mexico, Ireland, and Spain, have greatly expanded reproductive rights and abortion access.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，所有这些天主教国家——阿根廷、墨西哥、爱尔兰和西班牙——都大大扩展了生殖权利和堕胎获取渠道。

sentences.en: And even though overturning of Roe versus Wade just took away the national protection, a lot of blue states strengthened it.
sentences.zh: 尽管推翻罗诉韦德案刚刚剥夺了全国性的保护，但许多蓝州却加强了这种保护。

sentences.en: You know, so it's really how you tell the story, and there's a lot of different ways to tell it.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的取决于你如何讲述这个故事，而讲述它的方式有很多种。

sentences.en: So I always want to give people these broader perspectives, these deeper perspectives, this equipment for understanding
sentences.zh: 因此，我总是想给人们提供这些更广阔的视角、更深层的视角，提供一种理解

sentences.en: change in ways that empowers them to see it, to understand it, and to participate in it in ways I think you can't with the short-term perspectives.
sentences.zh: 变革的工具，使他们能够看到它、理解它，并以短期视角下无法做到的方式参与其中。

sentences.en: Do you think progressive change is inevitable?
sentences.zh: 你认为进步的变革是不可避免的吗？

sentences.en: I think nothing is inevitable, but I do think the word evitable should be used if we're going to use inevitable.
sentences.zh: 我认为没有什么事情是不可避免的，但如果我们非要用“不可避免”这个词的话，也许应该用“可避免”这个词。

sentences.en: In some ways, everything is evitable.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，一切都是可避免的。

sentences.en: We're deciding in the present what the future will be, and I think there's a lot of strengths
sentences.zh: 我们正在现在决定未来会是什么样子，我认为这里面有很多力量

sentences.en: and tendencies, but recognizing that the future does not exist really dismantles a lot of defeatism,
sentences.zh: 和倾向，但认识到未来并不存在，确实可以瓦解很多失败主义、

sentences.en: despair, doomerism, cynicism, which often pretend to know what the future can and can't be as a way of pretending to a power they don't really have while abandoning the power
sentences.zh: 绝望、末日论和犬儒主义。它们往往假装自己知道未来能怎样、不能怎样，以此来冒充它们实际上并不具备的力量，同时却放弃了

sentences.en: we really do have, which is to make a future that doesn't exist yet in the present.
sentences.zh: 我们真正拥有的力量，即在现在创造一个尚未存在的未来。

sentences.en: And I've spent my life listening to people talk about what can and can't happen,
sentences.zh: 我这辈子都在听人们谈论什么能发生、什么不能发生，

sentences.en: and usually not coming back to apologize when it turns out that actually Donald Trump can be elected, same-sex marriage is going to pass,
sentences.zh: 而当事实证明唐纳德·特朗普确实能当选、同性婚姻确实会通过、

sentences.en: we are going to stop the Keystone Pipeline.
sentences.zh: 我们确实将阻止基石输油管道项目时，他们通常不会回来道歉。

sentences.en: And sometimes when I want to be kind of an asshole, I'm like, wow, do you bet on the horses?
sentences.zh: 有时当我想要当个讨厌鬼时，我会想，哇，你会去赛马场下注吗？

sentences.en: Because you seem to be really good at knowing the future.
sentences.zh: 因为你似乎非常擅长未卜先知。

sentences.en: You know, I was just reading an essay by this writer named George Shialaba.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我刚刚在读一位名叫乔治·希拉巴的作家的文章。

sentences.en: I think he's one of the best political writers in America.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是美国最好的政治作家之一。

sentences.en: But he was pointing out that, you know, there can be a kind of value in certain forms of social conservatism.
sentences.zh: 但他指出，某种形式的社会保守主义其实也有其价值所在。

sentences.en: That sort of maintaining certain cultural or religious traditions, you know, it helps with social stability.
sentences.zh: 那种维持某些文化或宗教传统的做法，你知道的，有助于社会稳定。

sentences.en: It helps with inculcating large-scale trust among groups of people.
sentences.zh: 它有助于在人群之间培育大规模的信任。

sentences.en: But the problem, in this sense, I was pointing out, is when those traditions are based in illusions.
sentences.zh: 但他指出，这种意义上的问题在于，当这些传统建立在虚幻之上时就会出问题。

sentences.en: It's like an illusion could be the authority of white men, or that a certain kind of Christian morality is the only valid kind of morality, or that one's country can do no wrong.
sentences.zh: 这就好比幻想可能是白人男性的权威，或者是某种基督教道德是唯一有效的道德，或者是一个国家绝不会犯错。

sentences.en: But my question is, how do we promote stability and solidarity in the absence of the old illusions?
sentences.zh: 但我的问题是，在没有了旧有幻象的情况下，我们该如何促进稳定和团结？

sentences.en: I think that there are some really deep cultural traditions that are worth keeping, some of which are older than Christianity.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一些非常深厚的文化传统值得保留，其中有些甚至比基督教还要古老。

sentences.en: And one of the really magnificent things I see happening in the United States right now is the recovery of some of the really old stories.
sentences.zh: 我看到美国现在正在发生的一件非常了不起的事情，就是找回一些真正古老的故事。

sentences.en: And so I feel like part of the future, the best future we aim for is built by going back to the oldest stories,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得未来的一部分、我们所追求的最佳未来，是通过追溯到最古老的故事来构建的，

sentences.en: back to recognizing that patriarchy is not inevitable or natural or the only way people have ever done things, that there are in indigenous cultures,
sentences.zh: 追溯到认识到父权制并非不可避免、并非自然而然、也并非人们过去唯一的行事方式，在美洲原住民文化、

sentences.en: the Americas and Asian and African cultures, there are matriarchal traditions.
sentences.zh: 亚洲和非洲文化中，都存在着母系传统。

sentences.en: A lot of hunter-gatherers just seem to have a lot more gender equality.
sentences.zh: 许多狩猎采集者似乎拥有更高程度的性别平等。

sentences.en: So I think you can move forward with anchors in a deeper past and hope for a kind of stability and a deeper relationship to the old stories and the paSt.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，你完全可以带着对更遥远过去的锚定向前迈进，并期盼一种稳定感，以及与古老故事和过去的更深层联系。

sentences.en: But why is it that it feels so much easier to internalize the upsetting aspects, the retrogressive aspects of the world we live in, rather than the more positive context?
sentences.zh: 但为什么我们感觉内化我们所处世界中令人不安、开倒车的方面，要比内化更积极的背景容易得多？

sentences.en: You know, it's like we're more drawn to pay attention to the fire than to the place where there's calm.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就像我们更容易注意到火灾，而不是平静的地方。

sentences.en: I think you understand what I'm getting at with this question.
sentences.zh: 我想你明白我这个问题想表达什么。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: And in some ways, you're coming to the wrong person.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，你找错人了。

sentences.en: My friend Sam calls me the hope lady.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友萨姆叫我“希望女士”。

sentences.en: And I remain hopeful, partly as defiance.
sentences.zh: 我依然抱有希望，部分原因是对抗。

sentences.en: They would like us to surrender, to feel powerless, that there's nothing we can do.
sentences.zh: 他们希望我们投降，感到无能为力，觉得我们什么也做不了。

sentences.en: But I think the evidence speaks to that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为证据证明并非如此。

sentences.en: I think part of it that you're addressing is narrative itself on most stories are something goes wrong and then we have to address it.
sentences.zh: 我认为你所探讨的问题有一部分正是叙事本身，大多数故事都是某事出了差错，然后我们必须去解决它。

sentences.en: And when nothing goes wrong, there's literally no story.

sentences.en: There was this period a while back when people were kind of flouncing around with this, aren't stories wonderful?

sentences.en: And there are stories to justify white supremacy, misogyny, environmental destruction.
sentences.zh: 但也有用来为白人至上主义、厌女症和环境破坏辩护的故事。

sentences.en: The right has its stories, which the fact that this regime has to lie constantly says a lot about who they are.
sentences.zh: 右翼有他们自己的故事，这个政权不得不不断说谎的事实，本身就说明了很多关于他们是谁的问题。

sentences.en: But yeah, stories can be destructive.
sentences.zh: 但是的，故事可以是具有破坏性的。

sentences.en: A lot of stories can oversimplify.
sentences.zh: 很多故事会过度简化。

sentences.en: I do often see the stories people on the left tell.
sentences.zh: 我经常看到左翼人士讲述的故事。

sentences.en: And the left, I think, is a lot of different things, not a monolith, as very driven by their own version of sectarianism, grievance, often stories of oversimplification.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为左翼包含很多不同的东西，并非铁板一块，它在很大程度上是由他们自己版本的宗派主义、怨恨情绪以及往往过度简化的故事所驱动的。

sentences.en: Everyone in that category was like this and everyone in this category is like that.
sentences.zh: 那一类里的每个人都是这样的，而这一类里的每个人都是那样的。

sentences.en: And I talk a lot about the fact that categories are leaky and often see one of the jobs I try and do is just trying to give people more complex understandings.
sentences.zh: 我经常谈论的一个事实是，分类是有漏洞的，我常常觉得自己要做的工作之一，就是试图给人们提供更复杂的理解。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think the idea that stories are these magical devices that will do all our work for us is itself a bad story.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为“故事是能为我们包办一切的魔法装置”这种想法本身就是一个糟糕的故事。

sentences.en: But the story is often only the beginning.
sentences.zh: 但故事往往只是个开始。

sentences.en: When you change the story, that doesn't fix everything, but it often is the beginning of changing everything else.
sentences.zh: 当你改变了故事，这并不能解决所有问题，但它往往是改变其他一切的开始。

sentences.en: Rebecca, thank you very much for taking all the time to speak with me today.
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡，非常感谢你今天花这么多时间和我交谈。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: And I'm looking forward to talking to you again next week.
sentences.zh: 我也期待下周能再次与你交谈。

sentences.en: That was a wild gallop.
sentences.zh: 那真是一次酣畅淋漓的快聊。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: After the break, Rebecca and I speak again about what she wishes Democrats would do differently.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我和丽贝卡将再次谈论她希望民主党人做出什么样不同的举措。

sentences.en: I'm watching the left gear up to attack Gavin Newsom just in case he's the nominee in 2028.
sentences.zh: 我看到左翼正在厉兵秣马准备攻击加文·纽森（Gavin Newsom），以防他成为2028年的总统候选人。

sentences.en: And it kind of makes my heart sink.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到有点心灰意冷。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露（Winnalou）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》（Connections）这款游戏，它是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我也喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky and I create the game
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基（Sam Mazursky），我每天负责创作

sentences.en: Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 《拼写蜜蜂》（Spelling Bee）和《字母连线》（Lettered）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做通感（promesthesia）的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由刚才你听到声音的那些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Rebecca, I'm happy to be speaking to you again.
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡，很高兴能再次与你交谈。

sentences.en: Likewise, David.
sentences.zh: 彼此彼此，大卫。

sentences.en: What have you got for me?
sentences.zh: 你有什么要跟我说的？

sentences.en: You know, there's something that I said to you earlier that I've been thinking about and want to amend.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我之前对你说过的一些话，我一直在琢磨并想做个修正。

sentences.en: We were talking about
sentences.zh: 我们当时在谈论

sentences.en: green energy transition and how clean energy, you know, it's definitively on the rise.
sentences.zh: 绿色能源转型，以及清洁能源如何明显地在崛起。

sentences.en: And I pessimistically did some like, well, but kind of quibbling with that.
sentences.zh: 而我悲观地做了一些……嗯，算是吹毛求疵的质疑。

sentences.en: I was thinking about that.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考这件事。

sentences.en: I was like, well, that was a stupid thing to say.
sentences.zh: 心想：“嗯，我说那话太蠢了。”

sentences.en: Like, obviously any sort of clean energy transition is to be encouraged and every 10th of a degree of warming that we can prevent really matters.
sentences.zh: 就像，显然任何形式的清洁能源转型都应该受到鼓励，我们每阻止十分之一度的变暖都至关重要。

sentences.en: I think what got my back up a little bit when we were talking about that was this idea that
sentences.zh: 我想当我们谈到那个话题时，让我有点逆反心理的是这种观点：

sentences.en: somehow like the market will solve or help solve the climate crisis, even though the market is kind of the thing that got us into the climate crisis in the first place.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，市场会解决或协助解决气候危机，尽管市场本身正是把我们带入气候危机的罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: So I think that's where my comment was coming from.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我的评论就是从这个角度出发的。

sentences.en: I didn't want to come off like a kind of nihilist or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我并不想表现得像个虚无主义者或类似的人。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你。

sentences.en: I figured you were just playing devil's advocate.
sentences.zh: 我猜你当时只是在唱反调。

sentences.en: And yeah, I thought about that 10th of a degree thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想过那个十分之一度的说法。

sentences.en: And it's one of the complex things.
sentences.zh: 这是复杂的事情之一。

sentences.en: And I always feel like I'm asking people to go for nuance and shades of gray rather than black and white and the existence of contradictions and complexities.
sentences.zh: 而且我总觉得自己是在要求人们去寻找细微差别和灰色地带，而不是非黑即白，去接纳矛盾和复杂性的存在。

sentences.en: You really have to hold both, that there's still a lot to hope for, and there's a lot to mourn.
sentences.zh: 你真的必须两手抓：一方面依然有很多希望，另一方面也有很多值得哀悼的事。

sentences.en: And those things can exist at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这两者可以同时存在。

sentences.en: I feel like a lot of the trouble we get in is people who need those all or nothing stories.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们陷入的很多麻烦，都源于人们需要那种非此即彼的故事。

sentences.en: And they literally hear me too often as saying, if we're not losing everything, then surely you just said we're winning everything.
sentences.zh: 他们字面意思上经常误解我的话，以为如果不是一切皆输，那你就是在说我们赢得了一切。

sentences.en: And I'm never saying that.
sentences.zh: 而我从来没有这么说过。

sentences.en: And so you can be kind of heartbroken and exhilarated about climate at the same time and show up and keep doing the work, which keeps getting
sentences.zh: 所以你既可以对气候问题感到心碎，同时又感到振奋，然后依然挺身而出，继续做这项工作——尽管这项工作正遭到很多阻力，包括来自美国现任这个可怕政府的阻力。

sentences.en: done with a lot of pushback, including from the current horrendous administration here in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国现任这个可怕政府的阻力。

sentences.en: Well, whether it's to do with environmental degradation or degradation of our politics or degradation of people, it really seems to me like the public is hungry for an individual
sentences.zh: 好吧，无论是关于环境退化、政治退化还是人的退化，在我看来，公众确实渴望有一个人能成为对特朗普和特朗普主义的某种真正的抗衡力量或衬托。

sentences.en: to be some sort of real counterweight or foil to Trump and Trumpism.
sentences.zh: 对特朗普和特朗普主义的某种真正的抗衡力量或衬托。

sentences.en: And, you know, I don't know whether that person is Zoran Mamdani or Gavin Newsom is clearly trying to position himself as that person.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我不知道这个人是不是佐兰·马姆达尼（Zoran Mamdani），加文·纽森显然在努力把自己定位为这样的人。

sentences.en: I'd be interested in knowing your thoughts about him.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道你对他的看法。

sentences.en: But for whatever reason, that person has yet to be identified or yet to identify themselves.
sentences.zh: 但不管出于什么原因，这样的人尚未出现，或者说尚未表明身份。

sentences.en: Why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: I often think one of the great kind of weaknesses of our era is that we get lone superhero movies over and over that suggest that our big problems are solved by muscly guys in spandex whose superpower is ability to inflict and endure extraordinary violence.
sentences.zh: 我常认为我们这个时代最大的弱点之一，就是我们一遍又一遍地看着孤胆超级英雄电影，这些电影暗示我们的重大问题是由穿着氨纶紧身衣、肌肉发达的家伙们解决的，他们的超能力就是能够施加和承受非凡的暴力。

sentences.en: when actually the world mostly gets changed through collective effort.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，世界通常是通过集体努力来改变的。

sentences.en: It brings up something really beautiful that Thich Nhat Hanh said at some point before he died a few years ago, which is the next Buddha will be the Sangha.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起一行禅师在几年前去世前曾说过的一件非常美丽的事，他说：下一个佛陀将是僧伽（Sangha）。

sentences.en: The Sangha, in Buddhist terminology, is the community of practitioners.
sentences.zh: 在佛教术语中，“僧伽”指的是修行者社区。

sentences.en: It's the idea that we don't have to look for an individual, for a savior, for an ubermensch.
sentences.zh: 这也就是说，我们不必去寻找某个个人、某个救世主或某个超人。

sentences.en: Maybe the community is the next hero.
sentences.zh: 也许社区才是下一个英雄。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what Minneapolis is.
sentences.zh: 这正是明尼阿波利斯正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And I think the counter to Trump always has been and always will be civil society.
sentences.zh: 我认为，对抗特朗普的力量过去一直是、将来也永远是公民社会。

sentences.en: There's all this disparagement about wine moMs.
sentences.zh: 现在到处都是对爱喝葡萄酒的妈妈们的贬低。

sentences.en: And I read two things yesterday, one from the left, one in the New Republic, about centrists despising Trump resistance.
sentences.zh: 我昨天读了两篇文章，一篇来自左翼，一篇在《新共和国》上，内容是关于温和派鄙视特朗普抵抗运动的。

sentences.en: And those of us who are making a racket were often coded female as in hysterical, overwrought, need to calm down, no big deal, etc.
sentences.zh: 我们这些大声疾呼的人经常被贴上女性化的标签，比如歇斯底里、情绪过激、需要冷静、小题大做等等。

sentences.en: And the left also, you know, was taking some swipes at wine moMs. And, you know, a huge amount of the important work,
sentences.zh: 而且左翼也对爱喝葡萄酒的妈妈们进行了一些抨击。你知道，许多极其重要的工作，

sentences.en: I was thinking about this when I woke up in the middle of the night, is done by nice ladies.
sentences.zh: 我半夜醒来时想到了这一点，其实都是由善良的女性完成的。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people with platforms and a lot of the left want social change to look like, you know, the French Revolution or Che Guevara or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很多拥有平台的人和很多左翼人士希望社会变革看起来像是法国大革命、切·格瓦拉或者类似的场景。

sentences.en: And so the fact that nice ladies actually change the world, maybe it's about the fact that changing the world is more like caregiving than it is like war,
sentences.zh: 因此，善良的女性实际上改变了世界这一事实，或许是因为改变世界更像是照顾他人而不是像打仗，

sentences.en: but too many people still expect it to look like war.
sentences.zh: 但仍然有太多人期待它看起来像是一场战争。

sentences.en: And I denigrate politicians I don't respect as windsocks.
sentences.zh: 我把那些我不尊重的政客贬低为风向标。

sentences.en: I think a lot of our billionaires are also windsocks.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们的许多亿万富翁也是风向标。

sentences.en: They looked liberal when Obama was president and being liberal got you ahead.
sentences.zh: 当奥巴马当总统且当自由派能让你占到便宜时，他们看起来就像自由派。

sentences.en: in your pursuits, they now have become right-wing authoritarians because the wind's blowing in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 在你们追求事业时，他们现在已经变成了右翼威权主义者，因为风向变了。

sentences.en: If Trump falls and, I don't know, AOC or whatever becomes president, their wind is going to blow in another direction.
sentences.zh: 如果特朗普倒台，然后，我不知道，AOC或者其他人当上总统，他们的风向又会吹向另一个方向。

sentences.en: But I just want us to understand that most of the important change is collective.
sentences.zh: 但我只是希望我们能明白，绝大多数重要的变革都是集体完成的。

sentences.en: Do you think Governor Newsom is a windsock?
sentences.zh: 你觉得纽森州长是个风向标吗？

sentences.en: Not exactly.
sentences.zh: 不完全是。

sentences.en: I do think he's, you know, I think his trying to counter Trump by
sentences.zh: 我的确觉得他，你知道，我觉得他试图通过

sentences.en: making fun of Trump by sounding like Trump might have had its moment.
sentences.zh: 模仿特朗普的语气来取笑特朗普，这种做法可能曾经有过它的效用。

sentences.en: But it's also one of those things I'm watching the left gear up to attack Gavin Newsom just in case he's the nominee in 2028.
sentences.zh: 但这也属于那种让我注意到左翼正在摩拳擦掌准备攻击加文·纽森的情况，以防他成为2028年的总统候选人。

sentences.en: And it kind of makes my heart sink because I watch people tear down Al Gore.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到有些心酸，因为我看着人们毁掉阿尔·戈尔。

sentences.en: I watch people tear down Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 我看着人们毁掉希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: I watch people tear down
sentences.zh: 我看着人们毁掉

sentences.en: Joe Biden and Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登和卡玛拉·哈里斯。

sentences.en: And there's definitely major things to critique about every one of them.
sentences.zh: 他们每个人身上确实都有很多重大的问题值得批评。

sentences.en: But at the moment when, you know, like the job is to defeat the other guy,
sentences.zh: 但当任务本该是击败另一个人时，

sentences.en: you know, we defeat ourselves when that's what happens.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当这种事发生时，我们其实是在打败我们自己。

sentences.en: I want to go back to your new book for a second.
sentences.zh: 我想稍微回到你的新书上来。

sentences.en: So the new book is kind of about the inevitability of social and political change.
sentences.zh: 所以这本新书有点像是关于社会和政治变革的不可避免性。

sentences.en: But there's also an inevitability to personal change in all our lives.
sentences.zh: 但我们每个人的生活中也存在着个人变革的不可避免性。

sentences.en: Has there been a personal change that you went through that affected how you think about or respond to bigger change in the world?
sentences.zh: 你是否经历过某种个人变革，从而影响了你对世界更大变革的思考或反应方式？

sentences.en: There's so many of them that it's hard to pick out one.
sentences.zh: 这样的事情太多了，很难挑出其中一个。

sentences.en: I have an interesting experience every now and again that I think a lot of people have, especially if you're old enough to remember the 80s and the 90s, let alone the 70s.
sentences.zh: 我偶尔会有一些有趣的经历，我想很多人都会有，特别是如果你经历过80年代和90年代，更不用说70年代了。

sentences.en: You go back to something that you remember fondly and you find out it's just racist or sexist or cruel in some way that we kind of didn't notice or have tools or language for that was normal then,
sentences.zh: 当你回想起某件你曾美好回忆的事情时，却发现它在某种程度上充满种族主义、性别歧视或残酷，而我们当时习以为常，却没有注意到或者没有相应的工具和语言，

sentences.en: that's not so normal and acceptable now.
sentences.zh: 而现在这种事已经不再那么正常和可以接受了。

sentences.en: And there's so many things.
sentences.zh: 这样的事情太多了。

sentences.en: I wrote this book about Purple Rain, which I loved when it came out in 1984 and tried to watch during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我写了这本关于《紫雨》的书，我在1984年刚上映时非常喜欢它，并在疫情期间尝试重温。

sentences.en: I love Prince.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢普林斯。

sentences.en: I love what feminist things the movie has.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这部电影中包含的女性主义元素。

sentences.en: But there's a lot of just big-time abuse of Apollonia, Prince's love interest, that was kind of played for laughs and normalized in that movie.
sentences.zh: 但电影中也有很多对普林斯的银幕恋人阿波罗尼亚赤裸裸的虐待，在当时被当作笑料并被正常化了。

sentences.en: and I just thought who was I when I was in my early 20s watching that movie without even the
sentences.zh: 我当时就在想，当我20出头看着那部电影时，我究竟是谁，甚至连去

sentences.en: language or the space in which to feel that that stuff wasn't okay because if it wasn't okay you
sentences.zh: 感受这些东西并不对劲的语言或空间都没有，因为如果它不对劲，你

sentences.en: were just at odds with the world you you know there's kind of no place to go with it so I
sentences.zh: 就只会与世界格格不入，你知道，你根本无处倾诉，所以我

sentences.en: probably just laughed along so yeah I think about you know I have changed so much and my change
sentences.zh: 大概也只能跟着傻笑。所以，是的，我想到了，我改变了那么多，我的改变

sentences.en: isn't really separate from the social change and in so many ways we've all been re-educated around so many or educated around so many things.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是独立于社会变革之外的，在许多方面，我们在许多事情上都被重新教育了或者受到了教育。

sentences.en: Can I just add, I'm a big Prince fan and I think
sentences.zh: 我能补充一句吗，我是普林斯的超级粉丝，而且我觉得

sentences.en: there's been stuff that's come out since he died about his treatment of women and also like you're
sentences.zh: 自从他去世后，有些关于他对女性态度的爆料浮出水面，而且就像你

sentences.en: suggesting the culture has moved in certain ways that cast his attitude towards women or what it seems like his attitude towards women was in a different light.
sentences.zh: 所暗示的那样，文化在某些方面已经发生了变化，这让我们用一种不同的眼光来看待他对女性的态度，或者他似乎对女性持有的态度。

sentences.en: How do you think differently about the art of someone like that now?
sentences.zh: 你现在对这样的人的艺术有什么不同的看法吗？

sentences.en: And it really depends.
sentences.zh: 这真的因人而异。

sentences.en: I don't think there's a man who made art before.
sentences.zh: 我不认为以前创作过艺术的某个男人——

sentences.en: If I had a wristwatch, I'd check it, you know, about 10 minutes ago who was not,
sentences.zh: 如果我有手表，我会看一下时间，大概在10分钟前——不是这样的，

sentences.en: But, you know, there's some, but you go back a certain amount of time and I don't know, I had a wonderful English professor, Dr. Pellin, who used to say,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，有一些，如果你把时间回溯到一定程度，我不知道，我曾有一位非常棒的英语教授佩林博士，他经常说，

sentences.zh: 我跟那个在电影中扮演他的恋人——那个中年男子的恋人的17岁或16岁女孩是同龄人。

sentences.en: And it creeped me out.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到毛骨悚然。

sentences.zh: 我感到十分排斥，从那以后我再也没有看过一部伍迪·艾伦的电影。

sentences.en: I want to read a line from your memoir, Reflections of My Non-Existence, and then ask you about it.
sentences.zh: 我想读一下你的回忆录《我之不存在的倒影》中的一句话，然后就此向你提问。

sentences.en: So the line is,
sentences.zh: 这句话是：

sentences.en: Sometimes now I envy those people who are at the beginning of the long road of the lives they'll make, who still have so many decisions ahead as the road forks and forks again.
sentences.zh: “有时候现在我会嫉妒那些正处于他们将要开创的人生漫长道路起点的人，当道路一次次分岔时，他们的前方依然有那么多的决定要做。”

sentences.en: You're no longer at the beginning of the long road of your life.
sentences.zh: 你已经不再处于人生漫长道路的起点了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Can you see an exciting or pivotal or momentous decision coming?
sentences.zh: 你能看到前方有什么激动人心、至关重要或意义重大的决定吗？

sentences.en: Other than refusing to ever do another book tour, no.
sentences.zh: 除了拒绝再做任何图书巡回宣传之外，没有了。

sentences.en: And, you know, I'm pretty happy with the path I'm on.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我对目前的道路相当满意。

sentences.en: And really, I grew up with people telling me to have low expectations for myself.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我成长过程中周围的人都叫我对自我抱有低期待。

sentences.en: My mom told me point blank that my writing was just a hobby when I was in my mid-20s and that I should just glom on to my lovely, successful boyfriend forever,
sentences.zh: 我20岁出头时，我妈妈直截了当地告诉我，我的写作只是一种业余爱好，我应该永远紧紧抓住我那个可爱又成功的男朋友不放，

sentences.en: who I was in the process of leaving.
sentences.zh: 而当时我正准备离开他。

sentences.en: My father told me the only advice he ever gave me, I think, was I should be a business major because I'd never make a living in the humanities.
sentences.zh: 我父亲给过我唯一的一次建议，我想，就是让我选修商科，因为我在人文领域绝不可能谋生。

sentences.en: And I didn't really expect to quite have the trajectory I did.
sentences.zh: 我其实也没料到自己会有这样的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: And so I'm kind of thrilled with it.
sentences.zh: 所以我对这一切感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: But you always have a little nostalgia, lots of points where you make decisions.
sentences.zh: 但你总会有那么一点怀旧情绪，总会有很多需要做决定的节点。

sentences.en: And just that so many of them are ahead of you.
sentences.zh: 而且有那么多决定都在前方等着你。

sentences.en: I think is both hugely burdensome and also really exciting for young people.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于年轻人来说既是巨大的负担，也是极其令人兴奋的。

sentences.en: I watch them decide who to marry, whether to have a start of family and how, choose their profession, choose their major in college.
sentences.zh: 我看着他们决定和谁结婚，是否以及如何组建家庭，选择自己的职业，选择大学专业。

sentences.en: I kind of hate the way people treat your later teens and your 20s as though it's all light and fluffy when it's tremendously weighted because you're making
sentences.zh: 我有点讨厌人们把十几岁到二十多岁的这段青春时光当作是轻松惬意、无忧无虑的，其实它分量极重，因为你正在

sentences.en: decisions about who are you?
sentences.zh: 做出关于“你是谁？”的决定

sentences.en: Who are your people?
sentences.zh: “谁是你的同道中人？”

sentences.en: What is your life going to be about?
sentences.zh: “你的人生将维系于什么？”

sentences.en: And even though they're changeable, they're often permanent decisions.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些决定是可以改变的，但它们往往又是永久性的。

sentences.en: You're hitting so many forks in the road and they're such big ones.
sentences.zh: 你遇到了那么多的岔路口，而且它们是如此重大。

sentences.en: And some of them are revocable.
sentences.zh: 其中有些是可以撤销的。

sentences.en: Some of them aren't.
sentences.zh: 有些则不能。

sentences.zh: 丽贝卡，非常感谢你抽出这么多时间跟我交谈。

sentences.zh: 我真的非常享受，也很感激你能接受采访。
